core_obligations: Set up the trace form (proof lines 2146-2154): for the finite separable extension of degree n the trace pairing is nondegenerate, so choosing a basis of the extension inside the target ring produces a nonzero element of the source ring, namely the determinant of the matrix of traces of products of basis elements.

Reduce to a finite modification (proof lines 2156-2172): for a normal modification of the spectrum of the target there is an admissible blowup of the source such that the strict transform of the modification becomes finite over it; after normalizing both, one obtains a commutative diagram in which the morphisms from the two spectra are normal modifications and the vertical arrow is finite.

Compare cohomology through the trace (proof lines 2174-2184): the trace on the fraction field extends to a map of sheaves on the source from the pushforward of the structure sheaf of the modification, and the map given by the trace against the chosen basis is injective because it is so generically; composing it with the map given by multiplication by the basis elements yields the trace matrix, so the cokernel of the first map is annihilated by the chosen determinant, and the resulting exact sequence expresses the first cohomology of the modification of the target through the first cohomology of the modification of the source and the torsion of the former.

Conclude (proof lines 2186-2190): the first cohomology of the modification of the source is bounded by the assumption that reduction to rational singularities is possible for the source, so it remains to note that the torsion in the first cohomology of the modification of the target is bounded, which is the content of the torsion-bounding lemma, completing the proof.
proof_roadmap: Use nondegeneracy of the trace pairing to produce a nonzero determinant in the base ring.
Reduce an arbitrary normal modification of the target to one that is finite over a normal modification of the source.
Express the target's first cohomology through the source's via the trace map and the comparison map, and bound the remaining torsion.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that if reduction to rational singularities is possible for a two dimensional local normal Nagata domain, then it is possible for a finite injective local extension with separable fraction field extension (statement lines 2138-2144). The proof (proof lines 2146-2202) uses the nondegenerate trace pairing to produce a bounding element, reduces to a modification that is finite over a modification of the source, compares the first cohomology groups through the trace map, and bounds the remaining torsion by a chapter lemma. H3: an original comparison of cohomology through the trace with a reduction of the modification, written out in full.
